messages:
ravi (Docs): quick flag: examples for /v1/generate show Rate-Limit header as "X-RateLimit" but server uses "X-Rate-Limit" (dash placement). Python snippet parses header name and fails.

hana (API): thanks, good find. link?

ravi (Docs): https://redwood.dev/api-ref#/generate/post in the response headers example.

kevin (SDK): that mismatch made our example code check the wrong header key and default to fallback rate-limit behavior.

hana (API): looks like a docs formatting change slipped during a previous refactor. runtime always returns X-Rate-Limit.

ravi (Docs): proposed fix: update header name in OpenAPI examples and in the Python/Go snippet to check for "X-Rate-Limit". add a one-liner note in the docs: "Header name uses dashes as X-Rate-Limit".

kevin (SDK): i'll make client tolerant: check both keys and normalize to `rate_limit` in client metadata. PR -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/214

hana (API): tiny middleware not needed since runtime is consistent, but i'll update the internal generator so examples use the correct header name. PR -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/api/pull/1059

docbot: docs PR opened by ravi: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/523

ravi (Docs): merged after quick review and updated Python snippet. verified snippet parses header correctly in storybook. docs deploy queued.

docbot: docs deploy scheduled (v2026-03-28-0900)."
